items.reasoning: There are 2^a auxiliary labels and 2^n system labels, so U has square dimension 2^(n+a), while its auxiliary-zero compression B and target A are 2^n square. With the stated column-vector convention B(i,j)=U((0,i),(0,j)). The scale convention A=alpha B gives B(i,j)=A(i,j)/alpha because alpha>0 implies alpha!=0, and the converse follows entrywise. The approximate contract is ||A-alpha B||<=epsilon in the Euclidean induced operator norm; at epsilon=0, norm nonnegativity and norm definiteness make this equivalent to exact equality. Positivity is stronger than the cancellation hypothesis: a nonzero real scale permits division, while positivity is the declared normalization convention. At alpha=0 the undivided equation merely requires A=0 and leaves B unconstrained, so the divided characterization is invalid. 'Not defined' is the usual mathematical-ratio convention here, not a claim that Lean's totalized field division raises an error. With n=0 the system is a scalar and with a=0 B=U; the formulas remain valid. The answer and all three rubric criteria agree. I inspected the complete candidate structures and projection definitions: approximationBound is deliberately an arbitrary stored proposition, so those records alone do not prove this analytic inequality for a concrete circuit. No optimal scale or implementation efficiency follows. la-004 shares dimension/indexing prerequisites but asks a different representation equality, and la-008 asks a clean-action equivalence rather than normalization/error semantics.

items.reasoning: The stage/register description matches the source: selectorLift PREPARE acts on selector alone; AMPLITUDE changes the coefficient register controlled by selector and system; SELECT preserves coefficient/selector and permutes the system; the defined final stage is PREPARE-dagger on the same selector. For that definition the clean bra supplies conjugate PREPARE amplitudes and produces the intended squared selector weights. But the answer strengthens this sufficient architectural choice into 'only PREPARE-dagger' can recombine the weights and says the ancilla 'must return to zero' without separating clean projection from deterministic cleanup. The exclusivity is false: if P is PREPARE and D is any selector unitary whose clean row is <0| (for example diag(1,exp(i phi)) on a two-dimensional selector), then the different final gate Q=D P^dagger has the same clean bra <0|Q=<0|P^dagger and yields exactly the same projected LCU block. Even P=I with all intervening stages I and Q=diag(1,-1) is a different final gate with the intended clean action. Also P^dagger after a nontrivial SELECT need not return the selector to zero on the entire state: with selector P=H, a one-qubit system initialized at |0>, and SELECT choosing I or X, the final state has a nonzero selector-one branch. The source proves unitary composition and a clean-entry formula, not zero success probability for other auxiliary values. Thus the record's register assignment is sound, but its stated necessity/cleanup explanation and rubric c3 cannot be accepted as exact mathematics. This finding does not reject the source's explicitly defined P^dagger construction. be-006 is a different task deriving its exact clean entry; be-002 is precisely the projection-versus-cleanup distinction, not an alias. No compilation, query or finite-bit guarantee follows from the logical lifts.

items.reasoning: Let p_j=P(j,s0), r_j(x)=rotation(j,x)(c0,c0), and pi_j be the SELECT system equivalence. The clean matrix entry from (c0,s0,x) to (c0,s0,y) is sum_j [pi_j(x)=y] conjugate(p_j) r_j(x) p_j. Expanding the products, selectorLift first fixes coefficient c0 and data x while providing p_j. AMPLITUDE keeps (j,x) and changes only coefficient. SELECT maps x to pi_j(x) without changing j or coefficient. Finally the clean P^dagger bra fixes output coefficient c0 and data y and contributes conjugate(p_j), eliminating every other intermediate index. This proves the formula with the input x, not output y, controlling the rotation, and verifies all three rubric criteria against complete helper and root source proofs. With unitary PREPARE, |p_j|^2 are normalized selector probabilities; a general complex r_j can encode signs/phases or attenuation, so the whole summand is not generally a probability. The purely algebraic source identity even holds without unitarity of P or the rotations, while its physical probability interpretation presumes the named PREPARE gate is unitary. In the specified P/P^dagger architecture the same column and its adjoint produce |p_j|^2; independent choices would in general produce cross-overlap weights instead. This does not mean no different unitary with the same clean bra can work, nor does it prove deterministic selector/coefficient cleanup or supply the missing target-specific weights/oracles. Chosen clean labels entail nonempty coefficient/selector carriers; an empty data carrier has no queried entry. be-004 asks stage roles and be-110 proves SELECT bijectivity; neither is the same derived clean-entry identity. No resource or primitive compiler theorem is inferred.

items.reasoning: The elementary Gram calculations are correct: for D=[[x,y],[y,-x]], DD^T=(x^2+y^2)I, so real orthogonality is equivalent to x^2+y^2=1. A real y exists exactly when |x|<=1, with y=+/-sqrt(1-x^2), and at |x|=1 it vanishes. But the answer and rubric c3 explicitly offer enlarging the signal register as an alternative to raising the normalizer for a scalar |c|>1. That is false in every auxiliary dimension: if J is the clean isometric embedding, then ||J^dagger U J||<=||J^dagger|| ||U|| ||J||=1. More signal qubits cannot produce a clean entry/block with magnitude/norm greater than one at normalizer one. The answer's own universal contraction sentence contradicts this offered remedy. There is also a carrier distinction: the cited scalarDilation accepts rational x,y. Extending the question to existence of a real y is valid mathematics, but a rational y need not exist for every rational |x|<=1 (x=1/2 gives y=+/-sqrt(3)/2). The assumptions' phrase 'Real rational entries' must not be used to claim that the rational source supplies those real square-root witnesses. The row-overlap lemmas only prove conditional algebraic identities, not a general real/rational dilation existence theorem or circuit synthesis. I therefore reject the exact answer/rubric despite its correct calculations. The final sentence also reverses the normalizer wording: it is A/alpha, the encoded block, that must be a contraction under the convention A=alpha B. be-003 concerns nonunique completions; be-105 concerns the differently signed proper rotation and its Gram criterion, so neither is an exact alias of this scalar-dilation/contraction task.

items.reasoning: The stated proposition to be refuted is reconstruction of ANY matrix with at most one nonzero in each column. For a finite nonempty row carrier and a support map chosen to pick that possible nonzero, this proposition is true: choose c(j) to be the unique nonzero row when it exists and any row for a zero column; set amp(j)=A(c(j),j). Then every off-support entry vanishes and oneSparse_from_support proves exact entrywise reconstruction. In the square n=0 case all indices are empty and reconstruction is vacuous as well. The answer's alleged counterexample has two nonzeros in column zero and therefore violates the very 'at most one' premise of the contributor's claim. It demonstrates the limitation of the formula on a non-one-sparse matrix, but cannot refute that claim. Rubric c1 positively requires this invalid form of counterexample, so this is a question/answer/rubric logical defect rather than merely incomplete exposition. If c is fixed independently of the target, even a one-sparse target can fail the specified location condition; the record must distinguish that fixed-c claim from existentially choosing a suitable support map, which the current wording and counterexample do not do. The zero-column example B=diag(0,3) with c(0)=0,c(1)=1 is reconstructed correctly and does show zero amplitudes are permitted. Its entry 3 is an arithmetic matrix example, not by itself a normalizer-one unitary block; reconstruction supplies neither normalization, a reversible location oracle nor an actual amplitude loader. Complete source definitions and the full support proof confirm these distinctions. No bounded neighboring task has the same support-map reconstruction question; this correctness rejection is independent of semantic deduplication.

items.reasoning: The column and row Gram expansions and the clean entry formula are correct for a bijection p:Fin n->Fin n. Distinct columns have disjoint indicator supports, every column has one unit entry, and a unique preimage supplies each row's diagonal norm. The product embedding is injective on system labels, so the clean block is 0/1 with at most one 1 in each column AND each row, hence a partial permutation. However, the item explicitly assumes a self-map of one finite basis and demands an explanation that injectivity alone is insufficient for the row Gram identity. In that setting every injective self-map is surjective by finite cardinality. Thus injectivity alone already implies bijectivity and both Gram identities; there cannot be the missing-row example described in the answer under the declared assumptions. The source separates an injective-input column lemma from a bijective-input row lemma as proof interfaces, but those signatures do not prove strict mathematical necessity of an additional independent premise. A genuinely rectangular injection or an infinite self-map would permit injective/not-surjective behavior, but both change the stated finite square contract. The answer and rubric c2 therefore teach a false implication boundary, requiring rejection. Also, the claim that no non-0/1 target can be encoded needs the unit-normalizer/direct-clean-block qualification: the raw clean block is 0/1, but under A=alpha B a positive rescaling alpha times a partial permutation is still encoded by the same U. Weighting/LCU is needed for arbitrary relative entries, not necessarily for a common positive scale. All calculations are rational matrix identities; unitary realization over complex numbers additionally uses their standard real embedding, not a primitive resource theorem. be-104 asks equality of compiled gate semantics with a reversible permutation matrix and be-110 asks selector-dependent bijection; they are distinct from this Gram/clean-subblock task despite sharing permutation prerequisites.
